rejections.reason: Why are you using exact shape I drew? My drawing was super rough, i expected you to take that as a guide not exactly.

patterns: A hand-drawn sketch is a GUIDE, never a template. User's words on r2-10: "My drawing was super rough, i expected you to take that as a guide not exactly." Redraw the IDEA; never reuse traced path geometry.
Smoothing a sketch means RECONSTRUCTING it — proper curves, deliberate stroke logic, real letterform proportions. Averaging the wobble out and keeping that outline is tracing, not smoothing.
Never reuse one outline across a batch. All 10 of round 2 shared the same traced S and all 10 were rejected.

ARROWHEADS MUST BE BUILT TO MATCH THE STROKE THEY END — proportional width, same cap language. r1-27 was rejected "Looks messed up." and uses `<path d="M 78.00 33.00 L 65.00 20.00 L 91.00 20.00 Z"/>` triangles on a `stroke-linecap="butt"` stroke.
Do not mix cap styles inside one mark. `stroke-linecap="butt"` beside round-capped or rounded-rect elements reads unfinished.

AFFECTED SIBLINGS, not yet judged: 20 round-1 symbols carry the same loose-triangle + butt-cap build — r1-03, r1-21 through r1-26, r1-28 through r1-40. Rebuild rather than fan out from them untouched.

INFERRED, ONE INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION — DELIBERATE-LOOKING BREAKS SURVIVE; IRREGULAR ONES DO NOT. Round 4's four silent rejects each add an asymmetry: r4-02 mismatched half sizes, r4-04 open unfinished outer ends, r4-06 halves shifted sideways out of register, r4-09 a node bridging the gap. Round 4's survivors are all regular: r4-01, r4-03, r4-05, r4-07, r4-08, r4-10. CONFIRMED ON A CARD I DID NOT DESIGN: r3-04 was rejected 2026-08-11T10:35:13, and it is the ONLY one of round 3's ten to be rejected. Its note reads "Drawn the way a typeface draws an S: smaller upper bowl, larger lower bowl, lighter stroke above and heavier below. Proper letterform stress, not a symmetric loop." — i.e. the single most deliberately uneven card in that batch. STILL NOT PROOF: r3-04 carried no tag and no reason, one confirming case is not many, and a competing explanation exists — its lighter upper stroke may simply fail at small size. Correct this rule if it is wrong.

CAVEAT ON r4-04: the user had picked r4-04 and built their own r4-04e1 from it. r4-04e1 SURVIVES. Rejecting the base may be housekeeping after moving on, not a verdict on the design. Do not treat the ring-and-arrows direction as dead.
A fan-out is 10 interpretations of the source's IDEA: 2 close, 4 reinterpreted, 4 bold departures. Never a parameter sweep.
Card notes must name the IDEA explored, not the number changed.
'too busy' — reduce element count (r2-01). The mark must survive at 24px with the letter still readable.

CONFIDENCE NOTE: of 16 rejections, only 3 carry design words — "too busy" (r2-01), the r2-10 sentence in rule 1, and "Looks messed up." (r1-27). One more, "Duplicate" (r4-04e1e1), is housekeeping and NOT a design signal; it is a visual copy of r4-04e1, measured at 35 of 115600 pixels different, 0.03%. The other 12 are silent. Everything inferred here should be corrected if wrong.
